instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a lobbyist as someone who receives economic consideration from a principal and whose duties include lobbying, with an additional 5-days-per-reporting-period requirement if duties are not exclusively lobbying, rather than covering anyone paid any amount without further conditions.

A principal must register only after exceeding $500 in a calendar year for nonexempt lobbying, and principals anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and then are not subject to licensing/registration/reporting requirements if the statement is true.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: No lobbyist-definition spending/expenditure threshold is stated in the provided sections; the 'lobbyist' definition in § 13.62(11) uses compensation and/or days of lobbying communications, not lobbyist spending, and no other provided section supplies a lobbyist-side expenditure trigger for registration.

The provided text contains only principal expense statements (§ 13.68) and does not include any lobbyist-filed expenditure report requirement, so the existence of per-expenditure disclosure thresholds for lobbyist reports cannot be determined from this bundle.

No provision in the provided sections creates an exemption from lobbyist licensure/registration/reporting based on a percentage of an individual's compensated time; the only time-related lobbyist definitional threshold is 5 days per reporting period (§ 13.62(11)).
